plan.G: Launch these four research trees once in parallel. After research closes, retrieve their measured code and evidence, then integrate promising mechanisms selectively; do not assume gains are additive. Edit only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json, preserving the fixed entry point, Particle layout, one-kernel interface, launch.json schema, and all stated input and numerical requirements. Freshly compile and run the full correctness checks for every integrated candidate. Independently confirm the final candidate against the best confirmed correct alternative using the prescribed fresh-data protocol, and retain the best confirmed correct program by geometric-mean kernel time for N=4096, 8192, and 16384. Do not launch further research or change the target, checker, compiler, or protocol.
plan.analysis: Choose N=4 for four distinct, plausible optimization dimensions: block-level source reuse, force arithmetic, AoS source staging, and launch/work mapping. The first focuses on reducing repeated source loads across targets; the third tests source transaction efficiency for the fixed AoS layout, not another tile-size sweep. The arithmetic tree isolates math changes, and the launch tree isolates mapping and configuration effects. The supplied baseline is valid and correct; its three recorded timing values average about 1.8535 ms, but the payload does not label per-size timings, so this is context rather than a bottleneck diagnosis. No candidate improvement is yet measured or independently confirmed. Every child must preserve all-size correctness, exact output masses, the stated tolerances and edge cases, and use only the permitted source and launch files.

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, investigate block-level shared-memory tiling of source particles so multiple target threads reuse each loaded source tile. Keep one output target per thread and preserve the baseline force arithmetic and self-exclusion initially, isolating the data-reuse change. Handle arbitrary N, tail tiles, synchronization, and resource limits safely; tune tile/block sizes and src/launch.json only as needed. Validate all correctness cases and compare the prescribed geometric-mean kernel time.
children.subject: Shared-memory source-tile reuse

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, isolate force-math improvements while retaining the baseline one-output-per-thread mapping and global-load strategy. Evaluate algebraic cancellation of the positive target-mass factor and direct reciprocal-square-root/inverse-cube formulations instead of sqrt-plus-division; do not enable global fast math. Retain or rigorously replace self-exclusion so the isolated-particle extreme-mass case cannot produce NaNs. Preserve masses exactly and validate the CPU oracle, tolerances, coincident positions, and zero/negative dt before comparing timings.
children.subject: Force arithmetic and reciprocal-square-root

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, investigate cooperative source staging that improves transaction efficiency for the required 28-byte AoS Particle layout, such as contiguous word staging/repacking for the fields used by the force calculation. Keep the scalar force formula and one-output-per-thread mapping unchanged to isolate the load-layout effect. Do not alter the host layout or add preprocessing; ensure accesses are legal and aligned, handle partial tiles safely, and compare against ordinary fieldwise staging rather than assuming coalescing gains.
children.subject: AoS source-load efficiency

children.objective: Optimize only work assignment and legal launch settings in src/launch.json, with the baseline interaction math and data strategy. Ensure the kernel covers every output exactly once for arbitrary N even when items_per_block differs from block; the fixed kernel signature does not pass items_per_block directly, so use a universally correct mapping based on available launch dimensions rather than assuming that value is an argument. Sweep legal block/items_per_block choices, handle tails, keep the exact three-key launch.json schema, and compare the required timings and correctness cases.
children.subject: Launch geometry and output mapping
